title: Justine
author: Marquis de Sade
current_text: In 1791, authorities in France suppressed Justine or the Misfortunes of Virtue.

verified_ban_rows.note: A translation of Justine was considered by the NZ Indecent Publications Tribunal in 1965; Juliette (1969) was held indecent except for bona fide students over 20.

title: On the Origin of Species
author: Charles Darwin
current_text: On the Origin of Species was banned from Trinity College, Cambridge, England, in 1859.

verified_ban_rows.note: Banned by Nazi regime for conflicting with ideological views on race and creation.

title: The Adventures of Tintin in the Congo
author: Hergé
current_text: In 2007, the Brooklyn Public Library removed The Adventures of Tintin in the Congo from public display and kept it locked in a back room.

verified_ban_rows.note: In August 2007 Congolese student Bienvenu Mbutu Mondondo filed a complaint in Brussels demanding the book be banned as an insult to the Congolese people. The case was transferred to civil court in April 2010; in February 2012 the court ruled the book would not be banned.

title: Call Me By Your Name
author: André Aciman
current_text: In January 2023 the book was permanently banned from libraries and classrooms in St. Johns County School District, and in September 2023 it was banned from libraries and classrooms in Matanuska-Susitna Borough School District.

verified_ban_rows.note: Russian online retailer Labirint hid the book from sale in December 2022 amid removals of books that mention LGBT topics (The Bell); distribution was restricted further after the November 2023 Supreme Court ruling designating the "international LGBT movement" as extremist.

Banned in Malaysia by the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) under the Printing Presses and Publications Act. Gazetted 2025-08-04 (P.U. (A) 247). Publisher: ATLANTIC BOOKS AN IMPRINT OF ATLANTIC BOOKS LTD. Language: INGGERIS.
Banned in Belarus by addition to the Official List of Publications Harmful to National Interests (Ministry of Information). Decision: 2025-01-24. Country of origin: USA. Documented by PEN Belarus.

title: The Decameron
author: Giovanni Boccaccio
current_text: The Decameron was placed on the Index of 1559 under the instructions of Paul IV, and its prohibition was confirmed in the Index of 1564.

verified_ban_rows.note: Listed on the Index Librorum Prohibitorum from its first edition in 1559. The Church objected to explicit sexual content and to Boccaccio's satirical portrayals of lecherous clergy. A bowdlerised edition approved for Catholic readers replaced monks with "hermits" and abbesses with "noblewomen." The unexpurgated text remained banned until 1966.
In 1939 a NZ magistrate found the Decameron indecent in a prosecution of a lending-library owner; the finding was overturned on appeal later that year.

Boccaccio's medieval novella collection was named in independent reporting on a list of roughly 252 titles pulled from major Russian online retailers in late 2024 under Russia's expanded "LGBT propaganda" law.

title: The Jewel of Medina
author: Sherry Jones
current_text: The government banned The Jewel of Medina in Malaysia in 2009.

verified_ban_rows.note: Banned in Malaysia by the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN) under the Printing Presses and Publications Act. Gazetted 2009-07-30 (P.U. (A) 271). Publisher: Beaufort Books, New York. Printer: Dicetak di Amerika Syarikat. Language: INGGERIS.

title: Sophie's Choice
author: William Styron
current_text: Sophie's Choice was banned in Lebanon for its positive depiction of Jews.

verified_ban_rows.note: Banned by censors working for the government of South Africa under apartheid for being a sexually explicit work.
Banned by the censors in the Communist People's Republic of Poland for its unflinching portrait of Polish anti-Semitism.

title: The Hunchback of Notre-Dame
author: Victor Hugo
current_text: The novel was placed on the Index in 1834.

verified_ban_rows.note: Added to the Index in 1834 for its portrayal of corrupt clergy and anti-clerical subtext. On the Index until 1966.
The 19th-century French classic was among the ~4,390 titles barred by Kuwait's Ministry of Information censorship committee (2014–2018).

title: Zhuan Falun
author: Li Hongzhi
current_text: The Chinese government banned Zhuan Falun and other publications on 24 July 1996.

verified_ban_rows.note: The Chinese government banned Zhuan Falun and other Falun Gong publications on 24 July 1996 (US Department of Justice country report).

Foundational Falun Gong text (1995) by movement founder Li Hongzhi. Reportedly prohibited in Iran in 2008 as part of broader restrictions on minority religious movements. Source is OneWorld (Dutch HR magazine) compiling banned books across jurisdictions — not an Iranian primary source. Iran also bans Bahá'í texts and other minority-religion literature under the same doctrine.

title: The Second Sex

current_text: In 1956, the Vatican placed The Second Sex on the Index librorum prohibitorum, its index of prohibited books.
